summary: Enable a bounded audio-retention sweeper and per-job deletion controls: default to short retention for generated briefings, delete expired R2 objects and D1 pointers idempotently, and expose a dashboard ‘delete now’ action. Keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry.
note: NOTE RE-DERIVED 2026-08-07. The previous agent's 4,452-char patch plan was DESTROYED when this entry was set to "implementing": scripts/harness-ledger.mjs status --note overwrites the note, it does not append. Every claim below was re-verified against the live files today; the headline claim holds and is worse than it was stated. HEADLINE (TRUE): the sweeper cannot clear a backlog. audioRetention.js:171-175 lists with limit Math.min(Math.max(n,1),100) and passes no cursor; store/jobQuery.js:8 JOB_LIST_MAX_LIMIT = 100 clamps it again, so raising the local constant alone fixes nothing. Ordering is newest-first on both stores (store/d1Store.js:566 ORDER BY created_at DESC; store/memoryStore.js:166). The sweep therefore only ever inspects the 100 NEWEST audio_capture rows — the ones least likely to be expired — and repeated runs never advance the window. A keyset cursor already exists and is plumbed through listJobs({before}) (store/jobQuery.js:19-37, used at server.js:1893); sweepExpiredAudio simply never passes it. OTHER VERIFIED GAPS. (2) AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_MAX_BATCH = 200 at audioRetention.js:32 is unreachable dead config given the 100 cap. (3) No scheduled invocation exists: cloudflare-worker/worker.js exports only fetch, wrangler.jsonc has no crons/triggers, and the sole caller is the manual route at server.js:2151. (4) Inert as shipped: wrangler.jsonc:34 sets AUDIO_RETENTION_SWEEP_ENABLED=false and server.js:2149 forces dryRun, so the deployed sweeper deletes nothing under any input. (5) Bindings are not threaded into either delete path: server.js:2151 and server.js:2834 call without bindings, and cloudflareBindings is only populated inside the Worker fetch handler — under plain Node deleteAudioCaptureObject short-circuits false (audioStorage.js:130-136), so the D1 pointer is cleared at audioRetention.js:141-147 while the R2 object is orphaned permanently, and the response still returns ok:true. (6) Non-atomic ordering: the R2 delete precedes the pointer clear, so an updateJob throw leaves a row addressing a deleted object. (7) In record mode with no store.deleteJob the object is already gone while the row keeps a stale audioRef; that branch has no test. (8) One R2 error aborts the whole sweep: audioRetention.js:195-204 is an unguarded loop with no per-item try/catch and no partial report. (9) NO owner-pin concept exists anywhere in cloud-relay — the entry's "keep owner-pinned items separate with an explicit expiry" is 0% implemented. (10) One global 30-day TTL (config.js:27-31, wrangler.jsonc:33); generated agent audio is an ordinary audio_capture row tagged role:reply (server.js:1075), so "short retention for generated briefings" is not implemented and there is no briefing concept in cloud-relay at all. (11) DELETE /v1/ops/history/:pipelineId/audio (server.js:1979-1995) never follows replyCaptureId, so deleting a run leaves the synthesized reply audio in R2 — and record mode destroys the only reference to it. (12) No dashboard reaches either delete route: src/ops/api.js has no audio DELETE and no retention call at all, so the "dashboard delete now action" does not exist in the frontend. (13) The read-only report at server.js:2115 hardcodes limit 100, so storedRecordings and expiredCount are structurally wrong past 100 captures. (14) The sweep report calls captures.length "scanned" (audioRetention.js:182,209), implying a full-corpus scan that never happened. NO DEFECT FOUND on clock/units: createdAt is ISO-8601 wherever written (jobs.js:20,34-35), parsed with Date.getTime (audioRetention.js:62) and compared against ms Date.now (audioRetention.js:78,86); maxAgeMs is milliseconds in config.js:27, in wrangler.jsonc:33 (2592000000 = 30d) and in the comparison alike. TEST GAPS: audioRetention.test.js never exercises a backlog >100 through a real store (the batch-cap test calls selectExpiredAudioCaptures on a plain array, bypassing listJobs, so gap 1 is invisible to the suite and gap 2 is asserted as correct), never makes an R2 delete throw, and always passes bindings explicitly — which is precisely what production does not do. cloud-relay/ was NOT edited. Left proposed.
